I'll think this through as the farmer, then give the plan.

---

My reasoning:

I have 7 mu and two mouths to feed plus some money to make. Last year chili and cabbage on the same ground gave me the best money, so I keep that rotation on about 3 mu — chili goes in spring, cabbage after it in autumn. Maize I plant on 3 mu because the ground is a bit sandier there and maize does not need as much care as chili. The last 1 mu near the well I use for spinach — short crop, I can sell it quick or eat it at home.

For fertilizer I buy what the dealer in town sells — 15-15-15 compound and urea. Chili eats a lot, my neighbor Old Wang always says "chili drinks fertilizer like water," so I put down 2 bags of compound before transplanting and top-dress with 1 bag urea per mu when the fruit sets. If I short the chili, the fruit stays small and the buyer pays less — better to spend a bit more. Cabbage gets about 1.5 bags compound and half bag urea per mu. Maize I give less — 1 bag compound and half bag urea, like everyone around here. Spinach I just put half a bag compound, it grows fast anyway.

Well water is no problem so I water chili often — maybe every week when it is hot. Cabbage needs good water when the heads form. Maize I only water two, three times if the rain is short. Pesticide I spray when I see bugs — chili has aphids and that rotting disease, cabbage has those green worms every year.

Seeds I buy improved kinds from the dealer, hybrid for maize because everyone uses hybrid now. Tillage I use the small rotary tiller for vegetables, and for maize I plough deeper in autumn.

Yields — last year chili about 2500 jin fresh per mu, cabbage maybe 4500 kg, maize around 550 kg, spinach 1500 kg. I expect similar if the weather is normal.
